summary: CML urges the Commission to reject proposals that would terminate, significantly limit, or restrict E-Rate eligibility based primarily on geography. The text discusses the importance of E-Rate funding for libraries in providing connectivity and network infrastructure to meet the needs of their communities. It highlights the ongoing and continuous nature of connectivity requirements and the essential role of E-Rate in maintaining reliable internet and network services. The text also mentions the specific funding amounts received by the library for Category 1 and Category 2 support. Limiting E-Rate would disproportionately harm customers who rely most on library connectivity The text expresses support for preserving the E-Rate program and its need-based approach, emphasizing the importance of connectivity for schools and libraries. It urges the Commission to reject proposals that would terminate or substantially limit E-Rate and instead ensure that the program remains strong and available.
